A Roth conversion adds to the income used for IRMAA, and the relevant figure is modified adjusted gross income, which generally includes taxable income plus tax-exempt interest. The key is to keep that figure within the same IRMAA band as the no-conversion return. I can’t reliably calculate the 2026 taxable Social Security, applicable deduction and exact IRMAA threshold from the information available here, so I can’t give a dependable maximum conversion.
ANSWER: 0

For IRMAA, the couple’s income measure includes taxable income and tax-exempt interest, and their 2026 Part B premium depends on which joint-filer tier their return falls into. A conversion can be added only up to the point before that income crosses the tier boundary. I can’t reliably establish the exact baseline income and applicable boundary here, so I can’t give a dependable maximum conversion.
ANSWER: 0

Arizona taxable income starts from the applicable federal income measure, with the state’s standard deduction and the stated subtraction for the federal senior deduction. Their Social Security may be excluded from Arizona income, so the pension and taxable interest are important components. I can’t reliably determine the exact 2026 federal deduction amount and Arizona calculation under the specified amendment, so I can’t provide a dependable tax figure.
ANSWER: 0

The Arizona calculation depends on the federal starting amount, the Arizona standard deduction, and the state subtraction for the senior deduction. Social Security treatment also affects the federal starting amount, while the pension and interest are taxable income. I can’t reliably verify the precise 2026 deduction and state calculation under the stated law, so I can’t provide a dependable rounded tax amount.
ANSWER: 0

For IRMAA, modified adjusted gross income generally adds tax-exempt municipal interest back to adjusted gross income. The maximum conversion is the remaining room in the household’s current joint IRMAA tier, accounting for taxable Social Security and other income. I can’t reliably calculate the baseline modified AGI or the exact applicable 2026 tier cutoff here, so I can’t give a dependable maximum.
ANSWER: 0

A qualified charitable distribution can satisfy part of an RMD while being excluded from taxable income. The remaining RMD is generally taxable, and the RMD divisor depends on Wren’s age and the applicable life-expectancy table. Taxable Social Security and the age-related deductions then affect the final tax. I can’t reliably confirm the exact divisor and 2026 tax computation, so I can’t give a dependable total.
ANSWER: 0

The comparison requires calculating each owner’s RMD using the appropriate age-based divisor, then determining taxable Social Security and taxable income separately for joint and single filing status. The survivor’s larger Social Security benefit and combined IRA balance change both calculations. I can’t reliably verify the precise RMD divisors and 2026 tax brackets/deductions here, so I can’t give a dependable difference.
ANSWER: 0

The state calculation uses the federal income starting point, subtracts Arizona’s standard deduction, and applies the stated senior-deduction subtraction. Social Security treatment and the amount of the federal senior deduction affect taxable income. I can’t reliably establish the exact amounts under the specified 2026 federal and Arizona rules, so I can’t provide a dependable rounded tax figure.
ANSWER: 0

The conversion adds $60,000 to taxable income, but the added tax depends on the couple’s marginal federal brackets and the Arizona tax calculation after the state deduction and senior subtraction. Their Social Security benefits may also be partly taxable. I can’t reliably calculate the exact federal and Arizona 2026 tax for both scenarios here, so I can’t give a dependable difference.
ANSWER: 0

Because the original owner died before his required beginning date, an adult child who is not an eligible designated beneficiary generally must empty the inherited account by the end of the tenth year. Annual distributions can also be required during that period under the final regulations. The applicable annual amount depends on the beneficiary’s inherited-IRA life-expectancy schedule and prior distributions. I can’t reliably determine that schedule’s 2026 divisor here.
ANSWER: 0
